Every career line, accolade, and peak season was parsed directly from the player's Basketball-Reference page (downloaded 2026-07-25; WebFetch was blocked with 403, so pages were fetched via curl and parsed from the career footer rows of the per-game and totals tables, plus the on-page accolade list). Positions and jersey numbers match the game's roster-gaps assignments and canonical retired/iconic numbers. Conventions: spg/bpg omitted for players whose careers predate 1973-74 tracking (Havlicek, Monroe, White, Dandridge, McGinnis) since B-Ref's career figure covers only the tracked portion; fg3_pct omitted where the career sample is trivial or predates 1979-80 (Yao .200, Dwight .214, Gobert .000, and all pre-three-era players). George McGinnis stats are combined ABA+NBA (842 G, 20.2/11.0), consistent with how the game's nba pool already includes ABA careers (Erving, Gilmore, Issel); his 29.8 peak is the 1974-75 ABA MVP season. Active-player stats (Tatum, Mitchell, Gobert, Zion, Banchero, plus Carmelo-era retirees) reflect B-Ref career rows through the 2025-26 season as published. Carmelo's num kept at 15 per the roster-gaps file (he is also identified with 7 from the Knicks years). Earl Monroe kept at 15 (Knicks retired it; Baltimore retired his 10). Downloaded HTML kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aarons-portfolio/40f05f7c-fc2c-5359-9419-6d1513a72770/scratchpad/prun/*01.html for audit.

All 25 assigned players delivered (11 WNBA, 3 world, 11 BIG3); none appear on the do-not-duplicate lists for their leagues. Basketball-Reference returned 403 through the proxy, so all career stat blocks were verified against each player's Wikipedia career-statistics table (WNBA regular-season career rows; NBA infobox career totals for BIG3 players), with BIG3 context from the BIG3/season Wikipedia pages plus web searches (big3.com, Bleacher Report, Yahoo Sports for Chalmers' 2025 title). Deliberate omissions rather than guesses: Skylar Diggins' reported career bpg (0.7) was implausible for a 5'9" guard and was dropped; Satou Sabally's peak season was dropped due to conflicting figures; Kenyon Martin's NBA games-played was not published in the source; Nate Robinson's BIG3 team could not be confirmed so teams is omitted; Ginobili/Gasol/Rubio world records carry accolades without career averages because no reliable published career international stat line exists (Ginobili's 19.3 ppg peak is his published 2004 Olympic tournament average). BIG3 tiers are BIG3-relative per instructions: five superstars added (Joe Johnson 2019 MVP+champ, Maggette 2018 MVP+champ, Kenyon Martin and Al Harrington co-captains of the undefeated 2017 champion Trilogy, Chalmers 2025 champion captain), fixing the zero-superstar Legendary pack problem. Every BIG3 career block is the player's NBA line, flagged in accolades as instructed. Jersey numbers and positions match the parent's slot assignments (all corroborated except Cambage, where Wikipedia's infobox note of 18 was overridden by her far better-known No. 8, and Stephen Jackson's 5, one of his four documented NBA numbers).

48 NBA role players/rotation pieces/specialists from the 1950s-70s, zero overlap with existing.json (nba). Every career line and peak season was scraped directly from the player's Basketball-Reference page (cited in source) during this run — including verifying league-leading claims (Nelson FG% '75, Siegfried FT% x2, DiGregorio FT% x2 + rookie assists, Steele steals '74, Buse steals+assists '77, Van Lier assists '71, G. Johnson blocks x3) via the league-leader markup on those pages. Peak = best NBA per-game scoring season with 30+ games (ABA season rows excluded). Caveats: (1) Basketball-Reference career pullouts combine ABA+NBA for Don Buse, Jim Chones, Steve Mix, and Wali Jones (each had ABA stints), so their career lines include those seasons; (2) jersey numbers included only where confirmed (retired/honored numbers, or web-verified: Luke Jackson 54, Meminger 7, McMillian 5) — omitted everywhere else rather than guessed; (3) steals/blocks and 3P% omitted throughout per era rules. Tier spread: 34 role, 12 starter, 2 deep; positions PG 9 / SG 9 / SF 8 / PF 12 / C 10; decades: nine 1950s-era players, the rest split across the 60s and 70s. Borderline-tier calls made honestly: Sloan, Van Lier, Buse (multi-All-Defense types) tiered 'starter' not 'allstar' since they were stoppers, not stars. Sources: individual basketball-reference.com player pages listed per record.

55 NBA depth players from the 1980s-1990s: enforcers and Bad Boys pieces (Salley, Edwards, Hastings, Haley), three-point specialists (Hodges, Tucker, Legler, D. Scott, Curry, Barros), defensive stoppers (Ehlo, Russell, Blaylock, Bol, Dudley), backup/journeyman centers (Kleine, Kite, Koncak, West, Longley), and Vinnie Johnson-type sixth men (Pierce, E. Johnson, Tarpley, Bailey, Hot Rod Williams), plus CBA call-ups who stuck (Starks, Childs, Adams, Legler). Every record's stats were verified against its listed Wikipedia article (fetched 2026-07-25); Basketball-Reference blocked fetches. FG/3P/FT percentages included only where the article stated them. Jersey numbers come from the articles' infobox number lists; num omitted for 6 players (Childs, Legler, Wedman, Dudley, Koncak, Kite) whose most-identified number was ambiguous. Kevin Duckworth famously wore 00, encoded as integer 0. Ceballos (23) and Dale Ellis (3) numbers are well-known Suns/Sonics numbers not explicitly listed in the fetched summaries. Tier spread: 22 starter, 28 role, 5 deep. No overlaps with existing.json nba list (checked; e.g. Vinnie Johnson, Michael Cooper, Rick Mahorn, Kurt Rambis, Will Perdue, Tree Rollins already existed and were excluded). Eras reflect decades with actual seasons played; boundary seasons (e.g. a lone 1999-2000 year) were not counted as a separate decade except where the extra decade is core to the player's identity (Salley's three-decade titles, A.C. Green's streak ending 2001).

52 NBA role/rotation players, 2000s-2020s, none on the existing.json nba list. All career stat lines (g, ppg, rpg, apg, spg/bpg, pts) were verified per player via live fetches of landofbasketball.com player pages, except Kyle Korver and J.J. Barea (landofbasketball URL 404 for Barea), which were verified via their Wikipedia articles — the source field on each record is the exact page used. Shooting percentages are omitted for nearly all players because the source pages did not display them (only Korver's career 3P% .429 was verifiable). Peak = best-scoring season as stated by the source; omitted where the source didn't give one (Korver, Evans, Looney, Przybilla, Haywood, Cardinal). Jersey numbers come from the source pages' number listings; where the most-identified number was genuinely ambiguous (Belinelli, Ellington, Tyus Jones) num is omitted per instructions. Mix: 18 starter, 32 role, 2 deep; positions 10 PG / 11 SG / 11 SF / 10 PF / 10 C; archetypes cover 3-and-D wings (Battier, Ariza, Green, Covington, Crowder, Finney-Smith), backup PGs (Livingston, Mills, Barea, Tyus Jones, Monte Morris), energy bigs (Faried, Evans, Varejao, Birdman, Taj), lob finishers/rim protectors (Chandler, Biyombo, Przybilla, Looney), corner/movement shooters (Korver, Novak, Bonner, Ellington, James Jones), and beloved bench guys (Cardinal, Vujacic, Dudley, Nate Robinson, Pachulia).

44 WNBA depth records, every one verified against its Wikipedia article via live fetch this session (Basketball-Reference blocked automated access with 403s). No overlap with the 60 existing wnba names in existing.json. Spread: 1990s originals (Perrot, Hampton, Wicks, V. Johnson, Merlakia Jones, Mabika, Dydek) through 2020s role players (Dangerfield, Stokes, G. Williams, Sykes). Mix is mostly starter/role with a handful of allstar-tier non-superstars (Sales, Douglas, Phillips, Howard, Meesseman, Mabika). Jersey numbers included only where the fetched article stated one; omitted where ambiguous (e.g. Natasha Howard, Sugar Rodgers, Gabby Williams, Epiphanny Prince changed numbers across teams). Ruth Riley's num is 0 representing her signature 00 (schema requires integer). Career stats are the WNBA career-row figures reported by each article; fields the articles did not state are omitted. WNBA peak seasons use single-year format ("2015") rather than the NBA split-year format. Armintie Price is listed under her ROY-era name; her Wikipedia article is titled Armintie Herrington.

26 BIG3 records, star-weighted as briefed: 6 superstars (every non-excluded MVP — Beasley 2024+2025, Rashard Lewis 2017, Kevin Murphy 2022 — plus champion captains Jordan Crawford, James White, Gerald Green), 13 allstars, 5 starters, 2 role. Excluded per instructions: the 11 roster-gaps big3 names (Chalmers, Nate Robinson, Jason Terry, Joe Johnson, Al Harrington, Stephen Jackson, Corey Maggette, Amar'e Stoudemire, Jermaine O'Neal, Greg Oden, Kenyon Martin) — that removes MVPs Maggette (2018) and Joe Johnson (2019/2021/2023). Also skipped Cuttino Mobley and Mike Bibby (both notable BIG3 players but already in existing.json under 'nba'), and coaches (Lisa Leslie, Gary Payton, Nancy Lieberman, Julius Erving) since they were not BIG3 players. Stats caveat honored: BIG3 games play first to 50 points, so ppg is noted with that context in accolades; career pts totals come from LWOS's published all-time scoring list (through 2025). Jersey numbers given only where the player is unambiguously identified with a number (mostly their famous NBA number); omitted otherwise. Season facts verified against Wikipedia season pages (2017, 2018, 2019, overview), big3.com news posts, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report, and LWOS. Note for question-writers: the league rebranded to city-based teams in 2025 (Miami 305, Detroit Amps, Boston Ball Hogs, Chicago Triplets, LA Riot), and 2020 was cancelled (COVID) — no 2020 season exists.

World/FIBA expansion, 40 records, none duplicating existing.json's world list. Centers first per brief: Yao Ming and Pau Gasol fill the missing superstar-big slot, backed by dominant bigs across eras and continents — Krumins (USSR 1950s-60s), Loyzaga and Ramon Fernandez (Philippines), Wang Zhizhi/Bateer (China), Haddadi (Iran), Vujcic/Fucka/Vrankovic/Rebraca (Europe), Oberto/Splitter/Ayon (Americas), Mejri (Africa), Fajardo (modern Asia). Depth then spans Africa (Angola's Conceicao and Coimbra, Tunisia's Mejri), Asia (Shin Dong-pa, El Khatib, Jaworski), Oceania (Gaze, Palubinskas, Cameron), South America (Scola, Nocioni, Furlong), plus EuroLeague standouts (Printezis, Khryapa, Holden, Rigaudeau, Brody). Stats were included only where verified against live sources this session (Yao's 2001-02 CBA line via ESPN, Gaze's 18,908 NBL points via nbl.com.au, Haddadi's three Asia MVPs, Ayon's 2013 FIBA Americas MVP, Fajardo's record nine PBA MVPs, Fucka's EuroBasket 1999 MVP); all other records carry accolades only with unverifiable stat lines omitted. Jersey numbers included only where well-established (e.g. China's 13/14/15 Great Wall trio, Scola 4, Gaze 10, Jaworski 7, Fernandez 19); omitted where uncertain. Tiers are relative to international play, not NBA careers.

issues.name: Don Buse

issues.correct: career.rpg 5.8 if using the same full-career denominator as ppg/apg
